findings.title: Tapping a router tray chip places a stray router at the chip's map tile on release, consuming inventory
findings.location: app/main.odin:266-289 (release branch) vs :214-235 (press branch tray handling)
findings.evidence: Press over a router chip sets app.placing=tidx then returns. The LEFT-release branch has NO tray hit-test: `if app.placing >= 0 { if !moved { bus_submit(Cmd_Place_Router{pos={i32(wx)/tile_px,i32(wy)/tile_px}}) } }`. The release lands over the chip (same spot, !moved) → places a router at the world tile under the tray chip. Tray sits at win_h-36 → maps to an in-bounds map tile (separation-permitting) → stray router + stock consumed.
findings.detail: The flagship inventory interaction misfires on its basic gesture: a chip tap can drop a router you didn't intend and burn a unit of stock. Demolish refunds it, so not a soft-lock, but it degrades the ruling's feature.
findings.recommended_fix: Hit-test the tray rect in the release branch (skip placement when the release is over the tray), mirroring the press branch's tray_chip_rect check.

findings.title: Demolishing the bootstrap router refunds stock that was never charged — one free router_mid per run
findings.location: core/run.odin:55-66 (bootstrap_map spawn_node, no inventory charge) + core/topology.odin:325 (demolish `inv.routers[t.node_type[ns]] += 1`)
findings.evidence: bootstrap_map spawns a `mid` router via spawn_node directly (no inv.routers decrement). The tray seeds router_mid:1 from starting_inventory. Demolish unconditionally does inv.routers[node_type] += 1 → the never-charged bootstrap mid returns to the tray → 2 placeable mids.
findings.detail: +1 free hardware per run via demolish-rebootstrap. 'Redesign is the game' is intended; a free unit from the starting network is not. Single-player prototype, so an economy leak, not a soft-lock.
findings.recommended_fix: Either charge the bootstrap router against starting_inventory at run_init, or have demolish skip the refund for bootstrap-spawned nodes (a bootstrap flag).

findings.title: E9 drop ladder (BE→Standard→Express) is not implemented; per-lane queue shed can drop a premium packet while best-effort survives
findings.location: core/flow.odin:451-456 (per-lane `if idx_in_lane > queue_drop_depth` shed) vs spec E9 'Drop ladder BE → Standard → Express'
findings.evidence: Each lane is bounded independently by queue_drop_depth and sheds newest-first WITHIN the lane. The spec's E9 ladder ('contention drops by the full ladder BE→Standard→Express') implies premium traffic sheds LAST across the link. Under the implementation, an Express lane over depth sheds Express packets even if a BE lane is also full. The code comment claims Godot-reference parity ('the comment lied: newest-first').
findings.detail: Core QoS contract deviation on an edge behavior. The QoS system otherwise works (allocation, WRR floor, gap-fill, triage). Reachable under per-lane flood. Reframes the r1 W4 'shed order untested' residual.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement a link-level drop ladder (shed BE-class packets first when the link is contended), or document E9 as deliberately deferred to reference-parity and note it in the PR decisions.

findings.title: Run bootstrap allocates topology maps + flow/director arrays on the caller's heap; destroy frees only the arena → per-restart leak; flow_init sets context.allocator without restoring
findings.location: core/run.odin:77-101 (run_init_bare: make(map) under ambient heap; flow_init default allocator) + core/flow.odin:83-84 (context.allocator = allocator, no restore) + app/run/run.odin:90-104 (destroy frees arena_buf only)
findings.evidence: run_init_bare sets state.allocator=arena and make()s inventory on it, but `Topology{node_by_id = make(map[u32]u32)}` and flow_init's arrays (sla, roll_*, tick_*) allocate under the ambient context.allocator (heap at app create). run_context_destroy deletes arena_buf (wholesale) + snapshot arrays + autopilot_wired — NOT the topology maps or flow arrays → they leak per R-restart. flow_init does `context.allocator = allocator` with no defer-restore (latent pollution if ever called with an explicit allocator).
findings.detail: Re-opens the W7 class the r1 fix stopped: the SIGABRT is gone (allocators pair at delete), but bootstrap still splits ownership across heap/arena and destroy leaks the heap half. Bounded (~KB/restart), no crash; ODN-18 impurity.
findings.recommended_fix: Thread the run allocator into run_init_bare's map/array make()s (or set context.allocator=arena around bootstrap), and free the heap-owned arrays/maps in run_context_destroy. Restore context.allocator in flow_init.

findings.title: Hardware grants + Ev_Stock_Arrived have no direct assertion — the new inventory economy's only resupply is pinned only by the opaque surge_basics T1 golden
findings.location: core/run.odin:152-166 (grants apply + emit) + core/events.odin:36 (Ev_Stock_Arrived) + harness/demo_parse.odin:283 (valid_event_name omits stock_arrived)
findings.evidence: No unit test steps to a grant tick and asserts inventory deltas or the event; no demo's `expect event` can name stock_arrived (absent from valid_event_name). Grants DO land in surge_basics (ticks 600/1200/1800/2400) and ride the T1 hash, but only opaquely. Flagged independently by the tests lens on chunks a, b, c, e, g.
findings.detail: The ruling's flagship feature (hardware inventory) has its resupply mechanism unpinned at the assertion level. A grant that stopped firing, or fired the wrong tier, would pass CI as long as the T1 hash shifted 'consistently'.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test stepping to tick 600 asserting links[standard]+=2 + one Ev_Stock_Arrived; add 'stock_arrived' to the harness event vocabulary and an `expect event stock_arrived` to a demo.

findings.title: Right-click during router placement cancels placement AND cycles the hovered pipe's QoS priority in the same click
findings.evidence: The right-click handler (cycle_priority / open router popover) runs BEFORE the placement-cancel block. A right-click meant to cancel placement also submits a Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority (lands in the action log) if a pipe is under the cursor.
findings.detail: A cancel gesture mutates sim state (a logged command). Minor UI wart; deterministic, no soft-lock.
findings.recommended_fix: Gate the right-click priority-cycle on `app.placing < 0`, or move the placement-cancel check ahead of the priority handler.

findings.title: Logic/design cluster: empty-meter can end WON (win evaluated before lose on the surge-end tick; spec-silent on won-vs-lost precedence); multi-hop per tick / 0-latency same-tick delivery depends on pipe slot order; placement (euclidean²) vs growth (manhattan) spacing metrics differ despite the 'shared' E31 comment; neutral-tick max drain (carried); grace countdown dead (carried); pick_dst arena allocs (carried)
findings.location: core/health.odin:92-113 (win block before lose block) + core/flow.odin:406-474 (edge_idx advances within the tick's pipe loop) + core/topology.odin:262 (euclidean²) vs core/demand.odin:119 (manhattan) + core/health.odin:73 (neutral drain, carried) + app/render/hud.odin (grace '!', carried) + core/flow.odin pick_dst (carried)
findings.evidence: Win check `if h.prev_in_surge && !in_surge && !h.lost` runs, sets h.won; the lose check `if h.meter_pct<=0 && !h.won && !h.lost` then skips — a meter draining to 0 on the surge-end tick wins with an empty network (E17 only governs grace_expired suppression, not won-vs-lost). A packet crossing a pipe advances edge_idx and a later pipe in slot order can serve it again the same tick (0-hop latency, deterministic). placement_valid uses d[0]²+d[1]²<sep2; pos_free/min_dist_ok use manhattan — a player can place diagonally tighter than growth allows.
findings.detail: Spec-silent or carried corners. None break the fun gate (win/lose both reachable + tested; determinism intact). The empty-meter-won and multi-hop items are worth a design note for the A/B fairness read.
findings.recommended_fix: Gate win on meter>0 (or evaluate lose first) if 'Error 404 trumps' is the intent; decide one-hop-per-tick vs current and document; unify the spacing metric; (carried items per r1 fixes).

findings.title: CI downloads the Odin compiler tarball with no checksum; raylib still fetched by mutable tag (no commit pin)
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:38-41,51 (curl Odin release tarball, no checksum) + tools/build_raylib_sw.sh:13,25 (git clone --branch 6.0, a tag not a sha)
findings.evidence: CI `curl -fsSL $URL -o odin.tar.gz` with no sha256 check; build_raylib_sw.sh clones `--branch "$RAYLIB_TAG"` (6.0), not a pinned commit. A tag force-push or a compromised release would change golden/build bytes silently.
findings.detail: Supply-chain hardening; GitHub Releases + a release tag are trusted-ish and this is CI build infra (not the shipped artifact), so low risk. Extends the r1 raylib-tag-pin note.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin raylib to a commit sha + verify checksum; verify the Odin tarball sha256 in the CI install step.

findings.title: snapshot_write re-clones the inventory tray slices onto the heap every frame without freeing the prior clone — small per-frame heap leak
findings.location: core/snapshot.odin:97-98 (slice.clone(inv.links/routers, allocator)) called from resnapshot every frame (app/run/run.odin:104,109-115)
findings.evidence: resnapshot runs per frame; snapshot_write does `snap.inv_links = slice.clone(state.inventory.links, allocator)` reassigning a fresh heap clone — the previous clone is never deleted (~tens of bytes/frame, unbounded over a long session).
findings.detail: Small but unbounded heap growth on the hot path; ODN-18 'zero per-frame heap churn' violated for the inventory snapshot. No crash; ~5MB/hour at 60fps.
findings.recommended_fix: delete(snap.inv_links/routers) before re-clone, or reuse/overwrite the slice in place when the length is unchanged.

findings.title: growth_pool serialized without a length prefix; step-order header comment names topology_apply_all but the body applies commands one-by-one (carried doc drift)
findings.location: core/serialize.odin:170-173 (growth_pool loop, no w_u32 count) + core/run.odin step header
findings.evidence: `w_u32(&w, u32(d.growth_pool_idx))` then `for v in d.growth_pool { w_i32...; w_i32... }` — no count prefix, violating the 'lengths-not-capacities' T1 format claim (a pool-size change shifts bytes ambiguously; the golden compare still catches it). The step header references apply_all (batch) but replay applies entries in-order one-by-one (the pinned convention) — stale comment.

findings.recommended_fix: Prefix growth_pool with its length; fix the step header to describe the in-order apply.
